title: concise-technical-briefing-and-customer-timeline-2028-01-12
content:
Purpose:
This note is a customer-facing draft combining short status-page updates and a plain-language postmortem summary for customers impacted by the 2028-01-11 inference degradation in US-WEST. The goal is to give customers: (1) a timeline they can rely on for audits, (2) a short technical explanation they can pass to engineering teams, and (3) clear remediation/mitigation guidance.

Audience: Customer Success leads for enterprise customers, account teams, and engineering contacts who may re-use language on status pages and support replies.

=== Short status-page update snippets (copy/paste friendly) ===
Initial (first 30m):
- Summary: We are investigating increased latency and intermittent incorrect completions affecting text-generation in the US-WEST region. Some requests may return stale or duplicated content.
- Affected services: Hosted text-generation API (US-WEST) and some Dedicated capacity pools using the shared routing plane.
- Customer impact: Higher latency and occasional incorrect output; most requests still succeed.
- Action: Traffic is being routed away from affected nodes; engineering is actively investigating.

Ongoing (1–4 hours):
- Summary: Mitigations are in place and traffic is being gradually shifted to healthy capacity. We continue to monitor; a small percentage of requests may still see degraded output quality while failover completes.
- What we changed: Disabled canary autoscaler policy for the affected pool; reverted to last-known-good routing tables; applied KV-cache invalidation for stale prefix entries.
- Next update: We will post another update in 60 minutes or upon significant progress.

Resolved (post-recovery):
- Summary: Full service recovery confirmed for all impacted routes in US-WEST. Normal latency and correctness returned after controlled rollbacks and cache reconciliations.
- Customer impact: No lost customer data; resumed normal operation at 2028-01-11T21:34:00Z.
- Follow-up: A post-incident summary and recommended actions are being published to customers.

=== Plain-language postmortem summary for customers (short) ===
What happened?
- On 2028-01-11 between 19:03–21:34 UTC, a routing and caching mismatch caused a subset of inference requests in US-WEST to be served with stale KV-cache prefixes. This produced a small number of incorrect or duplicated completions and increased latency for affected requests.

Scope and impact:
- Affected customers: ~2.4% of requests from customers served out of US-WEST during the window. Dedicated customers with isolated pools were largely unaffected, except for some enterprise pools using the shared routing plane.
- Data exposure: No customer data was exfiltrated or modified. The issue was a caching/inference correctness problem, not a data breach.

Root cause (concise technical):
- A change to the autoscaler canary policy triggered rapid ephemeral node churn in a small pool. During the churn, the routing plane applied a partial routing table that did not match the active KV-cache state on some serving nodes. Because our runtime performs prefix-based KV cache lookup for autoregressive decoding, mismatched prefixes produced repeated or stale prefixes being reused for unrelated requests.
- Contributing factors: insufficient atomicity between routing table swaps and KV-cache version handshake; lack of an automated pre-swap KV-cache reconciliation step for canary-scale events.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Reverted the autoscaler canary policy and paused further canary rollouts to the affected pool.
- Deployed an emergency KV-cache invalidation job to reconcile prefix versions across nodes in US-WEST.
- Forced failover of traffic away from nodes that reported inconsistent prefix versions.
- Instituted temporary model-fallback to smaller, fully-pinned model variants for a subset of enterprise customers to preserve correctness while reducing exposure to routing instability.

How we verified recovery:
- Verified KV-cache version alignment across all serving nodes (checksum-based).
- Ran a synthetic prompt set (1500 prompts representative of customer workloads) and validated outputs against known-good baselines.
- Monitored production request traces and confirmed error/duplication metrics returned to baseline for 24 consecutive minutes before declaring recovery.

Customer-facing timeline (detailed):
- 2028-01-11 19:03 UTC — First alert: elevated latency and duplication errors reported by observability. Automated alert triggered.
- 2028-01-11 19:08 UTC — Initial mitigation: ephemeral capacity drained from pool; routing fallback engaged for a portion of traffic.
- 2028-01-11 19:22 UTC — Investigation: engineering identified correlation with canary autoscaler policy and node churn events.
- 2028-01-11 20:01 UTC — Emergency action: canary policy rolled back; cache-invalidator job queued and executed.
- 2028-01-11 20:45 UTC — Synthetic validation started (baseline prompt set). Quality metrics trending towards baseline.
- 2028-01-11 21:34 UTC — Recovery declared: traffic fully normalized; continued monitoring in place.

Planned permanent fixes and timeline for customers:
- Short term (next 2 weeks): implement an atomic routing-table + cache-handshake flow to ensure no partial table applies to live nodes; add an automatic KV-cache version check during any autoscaler-driven node handoff.
- Medium term (1–3 months): enhance the canary rollout orchestration to include a small-scale synthetic validation phase before new nodes accept live traffic; add additional tracing fields that let customers map any individual request ID to routing-version and KV-cache version for audit.
- Long term (3–6 months): improve routing-controller to support staged cache pre-warm and stronger guarantees for routing-table swaps; build a dedicated detection rule to block immediate canary rollouts if prefix-version divergence is detected.

Customer guidance / suggested actions for integrators:
- If you observed incorrect completions during the window, re-run critical prompts (we will persist request IDs if you need help correlating).
- For high-integrity use cases, customers can opt-in to model pinning or fully isolated Dedicated pools; reach out to your CSM for temporary pinning while we roll out the longer-term fixes.
- If you need postmortem artifacts for compliance, contact cs-legal@redwood.ai and include your account id; we will provide mapping of affected request IDs on request.

Internal notes to CS and account teams (do not copy verbatim to customers):
- Priority outreach list: top 25 enterprise customers by committed spend in US-WEST, then any accounts with active Dedicated pools that touched the shared routing plane.
- Suggested CS script: keep it short, emphasize absence of data loss, highlight options (replay prompts, model pinning), and offer a technical follow-up with engineering.
- Attachments to prepare: timeline CSV of major events, sample synthetic validation results, and a one-page engineering appendix that shows KV-cache checksum alignment logs.

FAQ (quick):
Q: Was my data exposed?
A: No. The issue affected caching and routing logic resulting in incorrect outputs for a subset of requests. There was no data exfiltration or permission change.

Q: How can I avoid this in future?
A: For workloads where any incorrect output is unacceptable, consider model pinning to Dedicated pools or enabling our safety/fallback policies that route sensitive requests to fully isolated capacity.

Q: Will there be compensation or SLA credits?
A: We will follow our standard SLA review process; CS will coordinate formal credit assessments for customers who qualify under their contract terms.

Contact and next steps:
- Primary contact (customer notices & follow-ups): Aisha Kapoor (Customer Success). Email: aisha.kapoor@redwood.ai.
- Engineering liaison for technical deep-dive: Marco Ruiz (eng-serving-runtime). Email: marco.ruiz@redwood.ai.
- Compliance/Legal requests: cs-legal@redwood.ai.

Note to author: this doc should be converted to two artifacts before publishing: (1) a 2–3 sentence status page update (use the "Short status-page update snippets" above), and (2) a 1–2 page postmortem summary for customers (extract the relevant sections under "Plain-language postmortem summary for customers" and the timeline). Tag PR to be reviewed by SRE and Eng-Platform before customer distribution.

End of draft.
